messages.subject: Re: Order L-36569 confirmed
messages.text:
Hi Anthony,

Storing the seeds in a cool, dark place was actually the right instinct, that part isn't the issue. The challenge with milkweed seeds is that they need a cold stratification period (simulating winter) before they'll germinate reliably in spring. If that step was skipped, most seeds simply stay dormant rather than sprouting, which explains the single sprout you got.

We'd like to send you a fresh batch of seeds that have already been cold-stratified, so they're ready to plant straight away with no extra prep. Given the timing right now in mid-July, planting outdoors this season is still possible for some species, or you can keep them in the fridge and plant next spring. Either way, we'll make sure you have viable seeds to work with.

Is the shipping address still the same one from your original order at [ADRESSE À CONFIRMER]? Just confirm and we'll get them out to you.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
